title: Highly active and selective oxygen reduction to H2O2 on boron-doped carbon for high production rates

authors.name: Xunhua Zhao

authors.affiliation: The University of Texas at Austin

abstract: Oxygen reduction reaction towards hydrogen peroxide (H<sub>2</sub>O<sub>2</sub>) provides a green alternative route for H<sub>2</sub>O<sub>2</sub> production, but it lacks efficient catalysts to achieve high selectivity and activity simultaneously under industrial-relevant production rates. Here we report a boron-doped carbon (B-C) catalyst which can overcome this activity-selectivity dilemma. Compared to the state-of-the-art oxidized carbon catalyst, B-C catalyst presents enhanced activity (saving more than 210 mV overpotential) under industrial-relevant currents (up to 300 mA cm<sup>-2</sup>) while maintaining high H<sub>2</sub>O<sub>2</sub> selectivity (85-90%). Density-functional theory calculations reveal that the boron dopant site is responsible for high H<sub>2</sub>O<sub>2</sub> activity and selectivity due to low thermodynamic and kinetic barriers. Employed in our porous solid electrolyte reactor, the B-C catalyst demonstrates a direct and continuous generation of pure H<sub>2</sub>O<sub>2</sub> solutions with high selectivity (up to 95%) and high H<sub>2</sub>O<sub>2</sub> partial currents (up to ~400 mA cm<sup>-2</sup>), illustrating the catalyst's great potential for practical applications in the future.

Highly active and selective oxygen reduction to H2O2 on boron-doped carbon for high production rates (2021) in Nature Communications is authored by Xia Yang, Xunhua Zhao and Chuan Xia. Topics: Boron, Carbon fibers, Oxygen, Reduction (mathematics) and Chemistry.

500 citations (OpenAlex). Citations peaked in 2024 with 124 citing works. Citing venues include Chemical Engineering Journal, Applied Catalysis B: Environmental and Angewandte Chemie.
